ZNP_WARM_RESET_SYS_PING_TIMEOUT.name: SRSP_SYS_PING_TIMEOUT

ZNP_WARM_RESET_SYS_PING_TIMEOUT.immediateMitigation: Verify rtscts matches your hardware (RTS/CTS DIO10/DIO11 is wired on SLZB-06U, SLZB-06P7U, and SLZB-06P10; set rtscts: false on SLZB-06, SLZB-06P7v1, SLZB-07P7, SLZB-07P10, and TCP bridges), verify /dev/serial/by-id/ path, or flash SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1).
ZNP_WARM_RESET_SYS_PING_TIMEOUT.remedy: Verify rtscts matches your hardware (RTS/CTS DIO10/DIO11 is wired on SLZB-06U, SLZB-06P7U, and SLZB-06P10; set rtscts: false on SLZB-06, SLZB-06P7v1, SLZB-07P7, SLZB-07P10, and TCP bridges), verify /dev/serial/by-id/ path, or flash SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1).

ZNP_0X11_BUFFER_FULL.name: BUFFER_FULL

ZNP_0X11_BUFFER_FULL.siliconRootCause: Exhaustion of NWK_MAX_DATABUFS or MAC_CFG_TX_MAX descriptors: on stock Z-Stack, slow-polling or offline sleepy Zigbee End Devices (ZEDs) can hoard nearly 100% of the shared nwkDB buffer pool (69 / 72 buffers) for up to NWK_INDIRECT_MSG_TIMEOUT (7.68s each), while O(N*P) per-frame flash security reads (22.19 ms per routed hop at D=150) stall TX pool drainage and starve outbound transmissions for the entire mesh.

ZNP_0X11_BUFFER_FULL.immediateMitigation: Use Zigbee Groups instead of firing individual unicast commands in loops, mark battery ZEDs as passive in availability settings, and stagger ZCL reporting queries.
ZNP_0X11_BUFFER_FULL.remedy: Use Zigbee Groups instead of firing individual unicast commands in loops, mark battery ZEDs as passive in availability settings, and stagger ZCL reporting queries.

ZNP_0XCD_NWK_NO_ROUTE.name: NWK_NO_ROUTE

EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.name: ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR
EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.title: Silicon Labs EmberZNet ASHv2 / NCP Fatal Desynchronization & EZSP Overflow
EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.description: The ASHv2 UART framing driver or bellows EZSP controller lost lockstep synchronization or overflowed packet buffers on the Silicon Labs EFR32 NCP (ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR / EZSP_ERROR_OVERFLOW).
EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.siliconRootCause: NCP packet buffer pool exhaustion (emFreeBufferCount == 0) or EUSART0 hardware FIFO receive overrun (EUSART0:IF.RXOF bit 3 asserted) during dense broadcast/APS storms when ASHv2 nRdy flow control or TCP-serial bridge jitter delays ACK frames past the adaptive ARQ retransmission limit.
EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.zeroStackFix: Verify physical UART/Ethernet link stability and hardware flow control settings on the EFR32 NCP. On SMLIGHT TI SimpleLink F2 coordinators, ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) provides DMA-driven UART recovery with 0 lost pings across hostile serial framing bursts (3-55 ms recovery vs 8.84 s blackout); EFR32 ZeroStack support is in active development. See https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack
EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.immediateMitigation: Ensure a stable wired Ethernet connection for network coordinators, use a shielded USB 2.0 extension cable away from USB 3.0 interference, and verify hardware/software flow control alignment.
EMBER_ASH_NCP_FATAL_ERROR.remedy: Ensure a stable wired Ethernet connection for network coordinators, use a shielded USB 2.0 extension cable away from USB 3.0 interference, and verify hardware/software flow control alignment.

EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.name: EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED
EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.title: Silicon Labs EmberZNet APS/MAC Delivery Failed (0x66)
EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.description: The EmberZNet coordinator transmitted the frame across all APS/MAC retries, but no acknowledgement was received from the target node.
EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.siliconRootCause: Caused by half-duplex 802.15.4 RF collisions from unthrottled ZCL reporting flooders, marginal link budget, or sleepy end-device poll timing misses when child tables and packet buffers are under heavy load.
EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.zeroStackFix: Throttle chatty power-monitoring plugs via ZCL Configure Reporting and add mains routers. On SMLIGHT TI SimpleLink F2 coordinators, ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1; EFR32 in active development) provides 135x higher routed hop security throughput (162 us vs 22.19 ms), eliminates flash-read stalls after FP=1 Auto-ACK during sleepy poll windows (82.7 us NWK encrypt, 6.8 us TCLK lookup, 0 flash reads), and enforces indirect queue quota isolation (50% pool cap, max 2 queued frames per sleeping child). See https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack
EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.immediateMitigation: Throttle chatty power-monitoring plugs using OTA ZCL Configure Reporting and add mains-powered Zigbee routers near low-LQI devices.
EMBER_DELIVERY_FAILED.remedy: Throttle chatty power-monitoring plugs using OTA ZCL Configure Reporting and add mains-powered Zigbee routers near low-LQI devices.

OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.name: OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT
OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.title: OpenThread RCP Spinel Timeout (WaitForWritable / HandleResponse)
OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.description: otbr-agent lost HDLC-Lite Spinel synchronization with the IEEE 802.15.4 RCP over UART/TCP.
OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.remedy: Verify UART baud rate (460800), disable software XON/XOFF flow control, verify hardware RTS/CTS wiring, and prefer a local USB/UART interface for OpenThread RCP.
OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.immediateMitigation: Verify UART baud rate (460800), disable software XON/XOFF flow control, verify hardware RTS/CTS wiring, and prefer a local USB/UART interface for OpenThread RCP.
OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.siliconRootCause: Host-to-RCP HdlcInterface serial framing stall, flow-control mismatch, or TCP-to-serial socket latency exceeding otbr-agent Spinel frame timeouts.
OTBR_SPINEL_TIMEOUT.zeroStackFix: Verify physical UART/USB HDLC-Lite/Spinel link integrity, disable software XON/XOFF flow control, and verify hardware RTS/CTS settings on the host border router. (Note: SMLIGHT ZeroStack Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1 is a Zigbee 3.0 / R23 Coordinator & Router firmware for SMLIGHT CC2652P, CC2652P7, and CC2674P10 adapters: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack).

flood.siliconRootCause: Unthrottled ZCL telemetry reports (e.g. Tuya TS011F / _TZ3000_ plugs firing at >0.5-5 msg/s) monopolize half-duplex IEEE 802.15.4 CSMA-CA contention windows and force legacy Z-Stack to execute O(N*P) linear flash log walks on every frame (532,182 cycles = 11.09 ms per NWK decrypt and 533,156 cycles = 11.11 ms per NWK encrypt at D=150), saturating CPU at ~45 routed pkt/s and starving host SRSP commands.
flood.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) executes per-frame NWK security in O(1) constant time with 0 flash reads (82.7 us encrypt / 79.7 us decrypt — 134.4x to 139.2x faster, >6,100 routed pkt/s ceiling) and cuts host serial reply latency by 83% (816 vs 4,921 cycles). Learn more at https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

delta-zero.siliconRootCause: Devices transmitting back-to-back identical ZCL attribute values (zero measurement delta) consume ~3.8-4.2ms of physical RF airtime per frame, trigger 11.09 ms per-frame flash security scans on legacy Z-Stack, and force redundant NV writes (100,714 cycles per write, triggering 163.9 ms flash compaction stalls every 69 writes).
delta-zero.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) delivers O(1) in-RAM NWK security (79.7 us decrypt, 139.2x faster) and idempotent NVM state deduplication (3,770 cycles with 0 bytes written to flash on unchanged state — 26.7x faster and 14.7x lower flash compaction rate). Details: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

mac-collisions.siliconRootCause: In stock TI Z-Stack, concurrent ED scans or channel noise can desynchronize background CMD_IEEE_RX from upper-MAC CSMA state (0xE1 / 225), while 11.11 ms per-frame flash security walks and 163.9 ms NV compactions after the 192 us FP=1 Auto-ACK delay indirect frame dequeue past sleepy ZED RX poll windows (0xE9 / 233).
mac-collisions.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) enforces self-healing Sub-MAC state recovery, O(1) 82.7 us in-RAM security (0 flash reads) during sleepy poll turnaround, and strict indirect queue quota isolation (50% pool cap, max 2 queued frames per sleeping child — Zero Battery-Device Bottlenecks) on SMLIGHT CC2652P, CC2652P7, and CC2674P10 adapters. Details: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

coordinator-buffer-overflow.siliconRootCause: Stock Z-Stack uses a first-fit variable-block OSAL heap (OSAL_Memory) that walks fragmented free lists (2,550 cycles at 64 holes) and fragments under concurrent unicast bursts (0x10 MEM_ERROR), while unpolled sleepy ZEDs hoard up to 69 / 72 nwkDB descriptors for 7.68s each (0x11 BUFFER_FULL / 0xF0 / 0xF1 / 0xB2 APS_TABLE_FULL / 0xC7 NWK_TABLE_FULL).
coordinator-buffer-overflow.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) provides constant-time O(1) memory allocation in 218 cycles (11.7x faster at 64 heap holes), heap-independent timer start in 1,448 cycles (6.9x faster), strict indirect queue quota isolation (50% pool cap, max 2 queued frames per sleeping child), and custom-tuned RAM/route tables up to 200-300+ source routes across SMLIGHT CC2652P, CC2652P7, and CC2674P10 adapters. Details: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

ash-uart-link.siliconRootCause: UART framing CRC/comm errors and serial disconnects occur when hardware FIFOs overrun during flash-erase interrupt masking or when hostile delimiter bursts / truncated frames lock up legacy Z-Stack's NPI parser for 8.84 seconds (44 lost pings).
ash-uart-link.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) provides hardened DMA-driven serial framing that recovers from 300x SOF floods, random line noise, and truncated frames in 3-55 ms with 0 lost pings and live auto-baud (115200 / 460800 / 1000000). Details: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

gentime-floods.siliconRootCause: Tuya and third-party devices polling ZCL Cluster 0x000A (genTime) in tight loops flood the coordinator with synchronous read requests, compounding SREQ/AREQ contention and burning 11.09 ms per frame in legacy flash security walks.
gentime-floods.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) processes NWK security in 79.7 us (139.2x faster) and APS security up to 75.5x faster (113 us vs 8.53 ms), preventing inbound ZCL genTime floods from delaying host commands. Details: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

aodv-storms.siliconRootCause: Each failed ping to an offline node forces the coordinator to broadcast an AODV Route Request (0xFFFC) that floods across every router. In a 50-router echo storm (1,000 duplicate broadcasts), legacy Z-Stack spends 3.00 ms per echo (3.00 seconds total CPU lockup), and a 64-frame broadcast flood saturates its 30-slot BTT (200.25 ms CPU).
aodv-storms.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) expands the Broadcast Transaction Table by +33% (40 vs 30 slots), suppresses 50-router broadcast echoes 20.3x faster (147 us p50 vs 3.00 ms; 151.16 ms vs 3.00 s total CPU), sheds BTT overflow 17.3x faster (174 us vs 3.01 ms), and scales Many-to-One source routing up to 200-300+ entries. Details: https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

issue-channel-mismatch.siliconRootCause: When host configuration forces an in-flight channel migration without ZDO Mgmt_NWK_Update_req broadcast propagation, sleeping end devices and routers remain stranded on the previous 802.15.4 channel.
issue-channel-mismatch.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack validates NVRAM channel invariants at boot (6.3 us key/descriptor reads, 213.9x faster) and executes deterministic Sub-MAC receiver and synthesizer recovery.

issue-adapter-discovery.siliconRootCause: Host USB/serial enumeration failed because the serial path symlink changed or container device passthrough is missing.
issue-adapter-discovery.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT SLZB coordinators provide persistent mDNS/TCP discovery and deterministic USB-UART bridge descriptors alongside ZeroStack's live auto-baud (115200 / 460800 / 1000000) and instant serial ping response (4,618 cycles). See https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack

issue-config-mismatch.siliconRootCause: Host PAN ID, Extended PAN ID, or Network Key in configuration.yaml diverged from the coordinator's non-volatile NVOCMP/NVM3 flash state.
issue-config-mismatch.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) enforces power-fail-safe NVM commits verified across 22,959 hardware power-cut points (0 lost records, 0 NOR verify conflicts, and 749x less post-brownout reboot flash I/O: 27 B vs 20,232 B). issue-pan-conflict.siliconRootCause: An active neighboring 802.15.4 coordinator or un-reset router on the same channel is broadcasting beacons with an identical 16-bit PAN ID.
issue-pan-conflict.zeroStackFix: SMLIGHT ZeroStack provides clean ZDO PAN ID conflict detection and deterministic channel/PAN migration without Sub-MAC state lockups.

issue-ember-ash.zeroStackFix: Verify EFR32 UART/Ethernet link stability and flow control settings. On SMLIGHT TI SimpleLink F2 coordinators, ZeroStack (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1; EFR32 in development) eliminates serial lockups with 0 lost pings across hostile UART framing storms (3-55 ms recovery vs 8.84 s blackout) and O(1) 218-cycle memory allocation. issue-ezsp-version.siliconRootCause: The Silicon Labs EFR32 adapter is running legacy EZSP protocol firmware (< v13) that lacks modern zigbee-herdsman ('ember' driver) and bellows frame control and callback framing.
issue-ezsp-version.zeroStackFix: Upgrade the EFR32 adapter to current EmberZNet NCP firmware (>= EZSP v13) via SMLIGHT SLZB-OS or Web Flasher. Note that SMLIGHT ZeroStack 0.9.9-beta.1 (Release Zero 0.9.9-beta.1) targets TI SimpleLink F2 ZNP coordinators (SLZB-06, SLZB-06U, SLZB-06P7, SLZB-06P7U, SLZB-06P7v1, SLZB-07P7, SLZB-06P10, SLZB-07P10 — not EZSP), while Silicon Labs EFR32 ZeroStack support is in active development (https://smlight.tech/software/zerostack).

issue-zstack-srsp.siliconRootCause: Multi-second NVOCMP flash sector compaction during zmain() startup (163.9 ms per page with interrupts masked) or hostile UART framing bursts desynchronize the legacy NPI parser for 8.84 seconds (44 lost pings).
